title: Adjacent Increasing Subarrays Detection I
statement:
`nums` holds `n` integers and `k` is a positive integer. Decide whether there is a start index `a` for which the two back-to-back blocks of length `k`, `nums[a..a + k - 1]` and `nums[a + k..a + 2k - 1]`, both fit inside the array and are both strictly increasing (every element larger than the one before it). Nothing is required where the first block meets the second.

Return `true` if such an `a` exists and `false` otherwise.
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every starting index `a` and comparing both blocks element by element costs O(n · k). Instead, remember for every index how long the strictly increasing run ending there is. A block of length `k` that ends at index `e` is strictly increasing exactly when that run length is at least `k`, so each pair of back-to-back blocks becomes two lookups.

## Approach

1. Set `ending[0] = 1`. For `i >= 1`, `ending[i] = ending[i - 1] + 1` when `nums[i] > nums[i - 1]`, and 1 otherwise.
2. The second block ends at `end`, from `2k - 1` up to `n - 1`, and the first block ends `k` places earlier, at `end - k`.
3. If `ending[end] >= k` and `ending[end - k] >= k`, both blocks are strictly increasing: return `true`.
4. If no `end` works, return `false`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [2, 5, 7, 8, 9, 2, 3, 4, 3, 1]`, `k = 3`. The run lengths are `ending = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 1, 2, 3, 1, 1]`. `end` starts at 5, where `ending[5] = 1` is too short, and `ending[6] = 2` fails too. At `end = 7`, `ending[7] = 3` and `ending[4] = 5` are both at least 3: the blocks `[7, 8, 9]` and `[2, 3, 4]` work, so the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass builds `ending` and one pass checks the block ends.
- Space: O(n) for `ending`.

## Pitfalls

- Nothing is required at the seam: in `[1, 2, 2, 3]` with `k = 2` both blocks increase although `2, 2` does not.
- Test `>= k`, not `=== k`: a longer run still contains an increasing block of length `k` ending there.
- Equal neighbours break a run, as the 4s in example 2 do.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `nums` |
| `ending[i]` | length of the strictly increasing run ending at `i` |
| `i` | index being extended while building `ending` |
| `end` | last index of the second block; the first block ends at `end - k` |

narration.4: Every element on its own is an increasing run of length 1.
narration.5: One pass measures the run ending at each index.
narration.6: Does nums[i] continue the increasing run that ends at i - 1?
narration.7: Yes: the run ending at i is one longer than the run ending at i - 1.
narration.10: Try every possible last index of the second block; the first block then ends at end - k.
narration.11: Both blocks increase exactly when the runs ending at their last indices are at least k long.
